title: The Notebook
briefing:
Three deaths in one night, the twenty-seventh of June, and one paragraph in the police file joining them with the word coincidence.

Naya, drowned in a basin of water in a locked room. Welch McGovern, at his own desk with the door bolted on the inside and no mark on him anywhere. And you.

In May, McGovern bought a black hardcover notebook — Ancient Feysac, a family dialect, and a grade the Church does not put in writing — and asked two friends to help him read it. It is not in his rooms now.

Captain Smith is giving the file to the probationer whose own name is already in it.

objectives.text: Establish how the rooms were sealed
Learn what actually killed three people

clues.title: The door was bolted from within
clues.text: A heavy iron bolt, thrown across and still in its housing when the police took the frame off. No trick of string throws that from the landing.

clues.title: The shutters were nailed shut
clues.text: Every window shuttered and nailed from the inside, and the nail heads are bright. He did this in the last week. He was expecting something, and not through the door.

clues.title: No wound, and no poison
clues.text:
No mark on him at all. The police surgeon looked twice because he did not believe himself the first time. A healthy man of twenty-six simply stopped, sitting upright, with his pen still in his hand.

Naya drowned in a basin she could have lifted her head out of. Nobody has written that sentence down next to this one.

clues.title: His watch stopped at 11:47
clues.text: Wound, undamaged, and stopped — not run down. The mainspring still has tension in it. Whatever reached this room reached the watch as well.

clues.title: Two cups, and only one drunk from
clues.text: Set out on the desk, both poured, one cold and full. McGovern had company, and his company sat through whatever came next without touching the tea.

clues.title: A page cut out of the transcription
clues.text: He was copying the notebook out longhand, bound in his own stitching, and one leaf has been cut close to the thread with something sharper than a penknife. Two words survive at the gutter. Neither is Loenese.

clues.title: Coal dust on the stair
clues.text: Tracked up from the cellar, dry, and laid down after the rain stopped at eight. Somebody came up out of that cellar late, and it was not McGovern, whose boots are clean and by the bed.

clues.title: The cellar hatch is bolted from inside
clues.text: The yard hatch, the one way in that is not the stair, fastened from the cellar side. Whoever used it drew it shut behind him.

clues.title: His money was not touched
clues.text: Eleven pounds and some silver in an unlocked box on the shelf, in plain sight of the desk. Nobody who came here for money would have left that. The only thing missing from these rooms is a black hardcover book.

clues.title: Something clings to the plumb
clues.text:
A copper weight on a waxed thread, lying where it fell. To an ordinary eye, a curiosity. To yours, it is still faintly warm in a way that has nothing to do with the fire, and it is still pointed at the chair.

This is what he divined with. This is the instrument, not the cause.

clues.title: The room remembers being afraid
clues.text: Not his fear. Fear does not print itself on plaster from one man. This is the residue of something that was afraid of what had been opened, and could not leave until it was finished.

clues.title: A second man waited in the cellar
clues.text: In the gap behind the crates: dust disturbed and then smoothed over, and the shape of somebody sitting with his back to the wall for a long time. Long enough to hear the whole of it through the floor.

clues.title: Franky will not describe the door
clues.text: He let the police in. He will tell you the hour, the weather and what he had eaten, in order, twice. Ask him about the door and he tells you the hour again.

clues.title: The police put it at midnight
clues.text: Sergeant Gorman's report says the surgeon put death near midnight and that the sergeant saw no reason to write anything else, which is a different sentence from agreeing with it.

clues.title: The bell rang eleven
clues.text: Two neighbours heard it from the landing and both are certain, and both are certain the light under McGovern's door was already out — which cannot be true of a man who died at midnight.

clues.title: Hanass says he was over the water by nine
clues.text: Straight from the last delivery to his lodgings across the Tussock, he says, and he can name the two people he passed. He offers the detail before it is asked for.

clues.title: The last crossing is at seven
clues.text: There is no bridge for four miles and the ferry stops at seven. Anybody on the far bank at nine either swam or was never on the far bank.

clues.title: He did not cross that night
clues.text: Sil Mowbray worked the boat and remembers the fares, because there were four of them and he had hoped for more. Hanass was not one.

clues.title: Alzuhod was buying it back
clues.text: Quill of Alzuhod, who arranged the sale in May and never handles the goods himself, has been quietly offering for the notebook again since the twenty-eighth — by description, not by name, and for a great deal more than McGovern paid.

deductions.title: Nothing left these rooms after they were shut
deductions.text: Door bolted, shutters nailed, hatch bolted. Every opening fastened from the inside. Whatever was in here when it was sealed was still in here — and Naya's room was locked too, and so was yours.

deductions.title: Somebody sat out the reading in the cellar
deductions.text: Coal tracked up after the rain, a hollow behind the crates worn by a man's back, and the residue of a second presence under the floor. He waited, he listened, and he came up afterwards for the book.

deductions.title: The notebook did it, and the plumb only opened the door
deductions.text: No wound, a room printed with a terror that was not his, and an instrument still warm and still pointing at the chair. He divined over the thing he was copying, and the thing answered — in three rooms at once, to three people who had read it.

deductions.title: He died at a quarter to twelve, not at midnight
deductions.text: The watch stopped at 11:47 and two neighbours put his light out before the bell. The surgeon's midnight is a rounding, and the quarter-hour it rounds away is the whole case.

deductions.title: Hanass sold it knowing what it was
deductions.text: One leaf taken close to the stitching, and the man who arranged the sale buying the whole book back at a price that is not a collector's price. Hanass was not disposing of a curiosity in May. He was moving something, for somebody, and he knew its weight.

deductions.title: Hanass was in the house that night
deductions.text: Two cups poured and one untouched, and a crossing he could not have made. He did not go over the water at nine. He went down to the cellar and stayed until it was quiet.

deductions.title: Nobody came here for money
deductions.text: Eleven pounds in an open box a yard from the body, untouched — and Mr. Franky, who will describe everything in those rooms except the way out of them.

resolutions.label: Name Hanass, and bring Smith the notebook
resolutions.summary: The whole account: the cut page, the cellar, the buyer, and the black hardcover book itself.
resolutions.epilogue:
You lay it out for Dunn Smith in the order a report wants it: the transcription first, then the ferry, then the cellar. He listens with his eyes shut and does not write a word, and at the end he says the notebook's grade before you have finished describing the binding.

Hanass says almost nothing, which is its own kind of answer. He waited under the floor because he had been told to make certain it was read, and he came up for the book because he had been told to do that too, and the man who told him has never once put his name to anything.

Old Neil seals the notebook in lead and lime and signs it into the Church's cupboard, and is quiet for the rest of the evening, which nobody here has seen before.

On the stairs, not looking at you, Smith says that three people read that book and three people died, and that the file has four names in it. And then he says goodnight.

resolutions.label: Take Hanass to the police and keep the rest
resolutions.summary: Enough for an arrest, and nothing the Church would have to act on.
resolutions.epilogue:
Gorman takes him, because you have given him a man who cannot account for an evening and a ferryman who can. It will hold. It will also be written up as a burglary that frightened a man to death, which is a sentence that means nothing and will be filed for thirty years.

You carry the plumb home in your coat and are aware of it the whole way. Smith notices you are carrying something. Smith notices everything, and says nothing, and that is worse than being asked.

resolutions.label: Give the Church the notebook and let the man go
resolutions.summary: The dangerous half, handed over whole. The man who moved it walks.
resolutions.epilogue:
You bring in the notebook, the transcription, and an account of the reading exact enough that Old Neil goes quiet halfway through copying it out. The Church would rather have this than a conviction, and says so in as many words.

Hanass leaves Tingen on the Thursday coach. Mr. Franky asks you, on the landing, whether anyone is going to be held to account, and you find that the true answer — that a thing is, and it has been put in a lead box — is not one you can say to him.

resolutions.label: Sell what you know to Alzuhod
resolutions.summary: He still wants the notebook. He would pay more for the man who lost it.
resolutions.epilogue:
Alzuhod's money comes in old notes, counted twice, through somebody who is not Alzuhod. The only question asked is where the book is now. You do not answer it. It is written down anyway.

The money settles the quarter with Mr. Franky and buys Melissa a term of books. You are aware, putting it on the table, that you have just become a man somebody keeps a page about — and that the last man who was that is the reason you live in this room.

resolutions.label: Report that you could not close it
resolutions.summary: No account, no arrest, no artifact.
resolutions.epilogue:
Smith takes it better than you had prepared for, which is its own kind of unpleasant. He says the first one is usually like this, and asks whether you have been sleeping, and you say yes, and he writes that down.

The rooms are let again by the end of the month. Nobody nails the shutters. The notebook is still somewhere, being read by somebody, and you will find out where when the file gets its fifth name.

leads.label: Ask along the Tussock wharf about the crossings
leads.description: Somebody on that river works every crossing there is. One of them will remember a fare, and all of them will remember the hours.
leads.successText: Three hands tell you the same thing without conferring, which is how you know it is a timetable and not an opinion: last boat at seven, no bridge for four miles, and a great deal of feeling about both.
leads.failureText: You buy two rounds and learn a good deal about a dispute over mooring fees. Nobody wants to give hours to a stranger who is obviously asking about hours.

leads.label: Pay somebody to name who is buying it back
leads.description: Somebody in the lower market always knows which gentleman has been overpaying, and he is always dearer than he looks.
leads.successText: A name that is not a name — Quill of Alzuhod, who arranged the sale in May, never handled the book, and has been offering for it again since the day after the deaths.
leads.failureText: Your money buys a name that turns out to belong to a fishmonger, and the pleasure of being told so afterwards by three separate people.

leads.label: Sit on the house from the coffee room opposite
leads.description: A night in a window seat with a cold cup, watching who comes back to a house where a man died with the door bolted.
leads.successText: At half past ten a young man tries the street door, finds it sealed by the police, stands in the rain long enough to be certain nobody is inside, and walks away towards the Tussock — the wrong way for a man who lives across it.
leads.failureText: Six hours, four cups, and a great deal of rain. Whoever was coming back had the sense not to come back tonight.

leads.label: Read the university and parish records
leads.description: Who matriculated with whom, who was sent down, and who has been signing for reading-room books he has no business with. Public, if you know which clerk to be polite to.
leads.successText: McGovern, Naya and your predecessor all read under Associate Professor Cohen, and all three signed the restricted room's book in May under a supervisor who had retired in the spring.
leads.failureText: The clerk is willing and the index is not. You lose an afternoon to a filing system that changed hands in the fifties and never recovered.

leads.label: Read up on divination by plumb and thread
leads.description: Old Neil's shelf has four books on divination by suspended weight. Three of them are wrong in ways he enjoys explaining, and the fourth is the reason the other three exist.
leads.successText: The thread is not the instrument; the thread is the leash. A plumb that keeps pointing after it has been set down is not answering the diviner any more. It has found something nearer to answer.
leads.failureText: You read for a whole evening and come away with a headache, a bibliography, and the strong impression that the useful book is the one Old Neil has not put on the shelf.
